To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) affective communication between individuals in a creative group facilitates the generation, selection and amplification of creative ideas, and (ii) the interface between individuals in a collaborative creative group can be designed to foster affective communication and therefore creativity.

1) affective communication is an important part of creativity in distributed groups; 2) affective communication in distributed creativity is enabled by a specific type of software interface; 3) the interface is a key parameter in a model of creativity in distributed, complex groups; and 4) affective communication can facilitate the generation of ideas, selection and amplification of the most promising ideas, and ultimately the creative product.

(1) the interface between group members is an important factor that can facilitate or impede the flow of information in a group; (2) affective communication is important in collaborative creativity, especially at the beginning stages of the process, when group members are getting to know each other and establishing trust; (3) group members who are more emotionally intelligent are more effective in the collaborative creative process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of affective communication in distributed group creativity, and the role of interface design in enabling affective communication.
how the interface can be designed and implemented to support the socio-emotional communication that facilitates the creative process.

the design of collaborative creativity systems, and we propose a new complex systems model for creativity in groups that incorporates affect and the interface between individuals, and which can be used to inform the design of such systems.
